newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 24.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 24.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

DUESSELDORF - Traditional advertising in Germany, Europe's biggest advertising market, will grow by three to five percent in 1997, says finance magazine "Wirtschaftswoche" based on a poll of advertising executives. The executives predict non-traditional advertising, including direct marketing and sponsoring, will grow by three percent this year.

OAK BROOK, Illinois - McDonald's Corp says its Big Mac sandwich will be the first of its menu items to feature in its rotating "Campaign 55" promotion. McDonald's 21,000 U.S. restaurants will sell the Big Mac for 55 cents when customers also buy any size drink and any size french fries.
LONDON - British outdoor advertising firm More Group Plc says overall performance in the first quarter was in line with expectations and the outlook for the second quarter is encouraging.

CHICAGO - Trans World Airlines Inc. plans to target business travellers this year with an expanded marketing programme offering first-class upgrades, preferred customer service, special amenities and better frequent flyer benefits.

FRANKFURT - Magazines and beer companies were the biggest sponsors of television broadcasts in 1996, says the Media Control research institute. Of the 16,800 sponsored programmes, almost 3,000 were sponsored by magazines and 2,800 by beer companies, says the institute.

WASHINGTON - Eastman Kodak Co and the National Geographic Society have forged a brand-marketing alliance to launch the Society's The Complete National Geographic: 108 Years of National Geographic Magazine on CD-ROM.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

FRANKFURT - Media distribution income is likely to shrink in the near future due to the free access to information available on the Internet, say experts at Frankfurt Marketing Services Fair. Print media representatives, however, say their publications will have a role in the distribution of information and opinions for years to come.

LOS ANGELES - Times Mirror Co says advertising revenues for Times Mirror's Newspaper Publishing Group for the four weeks ended March 30, 1997, increased 1.9 percent to $123,866,000 from $121,509,000 in the prior year.

HAMBURG - The German tabloids "Bild" and "Bild am Sonntag" said they had 11.26 million readers last year, making them the most popular newspapers in Germany, their publisher Axel Springer Verlag AG says.
PLEASANTVILLE, New York - Reader's Digest Association Inc plans to invest up to $400 million over four years in more aggressive publishing and promotion initiatives.
CANBERRA - The Australian government, under strong pressure from media giants, indicates it could ease media ownership limits.

TOKYO - Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. says it will begin to license linkage software for Video CD Internet, a new specification that enables users to view a Video CD on their computer and at the same time access related Internet Web sites.

WASHINGTON - The U.S. National Science Foundation, which funded much of the original research for the Internet, says it would now focus on scientific uses for the global computer network now that commercial demand is exploding.
BRAND NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

FRANKFURT - James Bond, Britain's famous screen secret agent, picks up keys to his new company car -- a $100,000 top-of-the-line BMW 750i saloon that he will drive in a new film "Tomorrow Never Dies", slated for release in December.
PARIS - Skip, a washing powder made by a French subsidiary of Anglo-Dutch giant Unilever, plans to launch a CD-Rom next month covering everything consumers need to know about laundry.
LONDON - United Distillers, the spirits arm of Guinness Plc launches a range of ready mixed cocktails called Tony's Freezer Cocktails, the latest in a long line of products aimed at young women.

SEOUL - Foreign carmakers, whose sales in South Korea have been hit by a "frugality campaign" which is designed to curb imports, say they are fighting back by opening more showrooms, cutting prices and introducing new models.

LONDON - British Airways Plc will unveil a new livery and corporate identity this summer. Chief executive Robert Ayling tells the annual convention of the Institute of Directors that BA is reshaping itself to improve customer service.
CHICAGO - Quaker Oats is likely to sell its Latin America pasta and canned fish businesses, as well as its U.S. coffee operation, analysts say.

SHANGHAI - The Shanghai Volkswagen Auto Co, a joint venture between Germany's Volkswagen and Shanghai Automotive Corp, has signed its first deal to export its Santana sedan cars, the Xinhua news agency says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

CARACAS - Venezuelan food consumption fell 24.8 percent in 1996 compared with the year before, according to a survey by local pollster Datanalisis. Hard hit by a stiff package of economic reforms, Venezuelans bought 34 percent less meat, 28 percent less fish and 12 percent fewer eggs, the poll shows.

HOUSTON - Anheuser-Busch Co Inc Chairman August Busch warns that anti-drinking groups want to impose a new Prohibition era on the United States. "There are those who would like see us return to that unsuccessful experiment called Prohibition. They are not looking for responsible consumption (of alcohol), they are looking for no consumption," he says.
